The invention relates to a method for producing composite webs or sheets comprising two metal cover layers and an intermediate plastic core layer. The plastic core layer is arranged between a lower metal cover layer and an upper metal cover layer and is integrally bonded to both, thereby forming a durable multilayer composite.

In a pretreatment line, each metal strip is continuously coated with an adhesion promoter to enhance bonding with the plastic core layer. Following this treatment, the coated metal strips are wound into coils for subsequent processing. The pretreated metal strips are then transferred to a separate laminating line, where they are brought together with the plastic web in the desired layered arrangement.

Within the laminating line, pressure and heat are continuously applied to the assembled layers. This process securely bonds the plastic core layer to both metal cover layers, producing a continuous composite web that may subsequently be cut or otherwise processed into composite sheets.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to a method for producing metal-plastic composite webs or sheets having two outer metal layers and an intermediate plastic core. In a first, separate processing stage, two continuous metal strips are each provided on at least one surface with an adhesion promoter. The adhesion promoter may be applied after suitable cleaning or pretreatment of the metal surfaces and is preferably dried or cured before further handling. The coated metal strips are then wound into coils and can be stored or transported to a laminating installation.

In a subsequent processing stage, the two coated metal strips are unwound and supplied to opposite sides of a plastic core layer, with the adhesion-promoter-coated surfaces facing the plastic. The plastic core may be introduced as a prefabricated film, sheet, or web, or it may be formed immediately before lamination. The layered arrangement is subjected to pressure and heat, for example by passing it through heated rollers or a press, so that the adhesion promoter bonds the metal strips firmly and substantially over their entire surfaces to the plastic core. After cooling, the resulting composite web may be wound, cut to length, or divided into sheets for further processing.

By separating the continuous pretreatment and coating of the metal strips from the actual laminating operation, the method avoids the need to integrate cleaning, coating, and drying equipment into the laminating line. The laminating installation can therefore be more compact and can operate continuously at a speed determined primarily by the bonding process. At the same time, the coated metal coils can be prepared independently and supplied as needed, improving production flexibility and reducing interruptions. The method consequently permits efficient, economical manufacture of dimensionally stable metal-plastic composite material with a durable, integral bond between the metal outer layers and the plastic core.

### The Power of “The”

“The” is one of the smallest yet most important words in the English language. Known as the definite article, it identifies a specific person, place, object, or idea. For example, “a book” can refer to any book, while “the book” points to one particular book already known to the speaker and listener.

Although it often goes unnoticed, “the” makes communication clearer and more precise. It helps connect ideas, establish context, and guide attention toward something specific. Its frequent use shows that even the simplest words can have a powerful role in language.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract describing a continuous method for producing a metal–plastic–metal composite web using separate pretreatment and laminating lines.
counterfactuals.output: A continuous method is disclosed for producing a metal–plastic–metal composite web using physically separate pretreatment and laminating lines. In the pretreatment line, first and second metal strips are continuously unwound, cleaned, chemically and/or mechanically pretreated, optionally coated with an adhesion-promoting layer, dried, and rewound to form respective pretreated coils. The pretreated coils are transferred to the laminating line, where the first and second metal strips are continuously unwound and supplied on opposite sides of a continuously advancing thermoplastic film or extruded polymer layer. The metal strips and the polymer layer are heated to an activating or softening temperature, brought together under pressure, and passed through a laminating zone to form a bonded multilayer web. The composite web is subsequently cooled, optionally edge-trimmed and inspected, and wound or cut to length. Separating pretreatment from lamination permits independent control of surface treatment and bonding conditions while enabling continuous, high-throughput production of a composite web having improved interlayer adhesion and uniformity.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention in which two metal strips are coated with an adhesion promoter, wound, and later bonded with a plastic core under heat and pressure. Include numbered reference signs.
counterfactuals.output:
**Invention: Method for Producing a Metal–Plastic–Metal Laminate**

A first metal strip **(1)** and a second metal strip **(2)** are continuously supplied from respective feed rolls **(3, 4)**. An adhesion promoter **(5)** is applied to one bonding surface **(6, 7)** of each metal strip by coating devices **(8, 9)**. After optional drying or curing in treatment stations **(10, 11)**, the coated metal strips **(1, 2)** are wound separately into storage coils **(12, 13)**. Winding allows the pretreated strips to be manufactured, transported, and stored independently of the subsequent laminating operation.

For laminate production, the coated strips **(1, 2)** are unwound from the storage coils **(12, 13)** and guided toward a laminating station **(14)**. A thermoplastic core layer **(15)**, supplied as a film, sheet, or extruded web from a core source **(16)**, is introduced between the coated bonding surfaces **(6, 7)**. The resulting layered assembly **(17)** passes through heated pressure rollers or a hot press **(18)**.

Heat softens or melts at least a surface region of the plastic core **(15)** and activates the adhesion promoter **(5)**. Simultaneously applied pressure brings the layers into intimate contact, thereby bonding both metal strips **(1, 2)** to the plastic core **(15)**. A cooling unit **(19)** subsequently solidifies the plastic and fixes the bond. The finished metal–plastic–metal laminate **(20)** may then be wound onto a product coil **(21)** or cut into panels by a cutting device **(22)**.

The prior coating and winding of the metal strips separates surface treatment from final lamination, permits long-term storage of prepared strips, and enables efficient continuous production of a lightweight composite having metallic outer layers and a plastic core.

counterfactuals.output:
### Exemplary Method Claims

1. **A method for producing a metal-plastic laminate, the method comprising:**

   continuously advancing a metal strip through a pretreatment production line;

   while the metal strip is continuously advancing through the pretreatment production line, subjecting at least one major surface of the metal strip to a surface pretreatment to form a pretreated metal strip;

   removing the pretreated metal strip from the pretreatment production line;

   transferring the pretreated metal strip to a laminating production line that is physically separate from the pretreatment production line; and

   in the laminating production line, advancing the pretreated metal strip together with a plastic web through a laminating station and bonding the plastic web to the at least one major surface of the pretreated metal strip, thereby forming the metal-plastic laminate.

2. **The method of claim 1**, wherein the pretreated metal strip is wound into a coil after removal from the pretreatment production line and is subsequently unwound in the laminating production line.

3. **The method of claim 1**, wherein the pretreated metal strip is stored for a period of time between the surface pretreatment and the bonding of the plastic web.

4. **The method of claim 1**, wherein the surface pretreatment comprises one or more of degreasing, cleaning, pickling, etching, conversion coating, anodizing, plasma treatment, corona treatment, flame treatment, application of a primer, and application of an adhesion-promoting composition.

5. **The method of claim 1**, wherein the surface pretreatment comprises applying a pretreatment composition to the at least one major surface and drying or curing the pretreatment composition before the pretreated metal strip is removed from the pretreatment production line.

6. **The method of claim 1**, wherein the metal strip comprises aluminum, an aluminum alloy, steel, stainless steel, copper, or a copper alloy.

7. **The method of claim 1**, wherein the plastic web comprises a thermoplastic polymer selected from polyethylene, polypropylene, polyester, polyamide, polyvinyl chloride, polycarbonate, and combinations thereof.

8. **The method of claim 1**, wherein bonding the plastic web comprises heating at least one of the pretreated metal strip and the plastic web and applying pressure to the pretreated metal strip and the plastic web.

9. **The method of claim 1**, wherein an adhesive layer is disposed between the pretreated metal strip and the plastic web before passage through the laminating station.

10. **The method of claim 1**, wherein the plastic web is bonded directly to the pretreated metal strip without an intervening adhesive layer.

11. **The method of claim 1**, wherein the pretreatment production line and the laminating production line are operated independently of one another with respect to at least one of line speed, production schedule, and process control.

12. **The method of claim 1**, wherein the pretreated metal strip is transported from a first manufacturing location containing the pretreatment production line to a second manufacturing location containing the laminating production line.

13. **The method of claim 1**, further comprising bonding a second plastic web to an opposite major surface of the pretreated metal strip in the laminating production line.

14. **The method of claim 1**, further comprising cooling the metal-plastic laminate and winding the metal-plastic laminate into a laminate coil.

### Exemplary Specification Language

In certain embodiments, an elongate metal strip is continuously processed in a first production line configured for surface pretreatment. The term “continuously” denotes movement of the metal strip through at least the pretreatment section as an uninterrupted web, and does not require perpetual operation or preclude temporary stoppage of the production line. Following pretreatment, the strip may be wound, accumulated, stored, transported, or otherwise handled independently of a subsequent laminating operation.

The pretreated metal strip is thereafter supplied to a second production line that is separate from the first production line. As used herein, “separate” means that the laminating production line is not arranged in-line with the pretreatment production line such that the strip passes directly and continuously from pretreatment to lamination. The respective production lines may be located within a common facility or at geographically distinct facilities and may be operated at different line speeds or at different times.

In the second production line, the pretreated metal strip and at least one plastic web are brought into superposed relationship and subjected to heat, pressure, adhesive activation, or a combination thereof to establish a bond between the plastic web and the pretreated surface of the metal strip. Separation of the pretreatment and laminating operations permits independent optimization, scheduling, maintenance, and throughput control of the respective production lines.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a technical invention summary for manufacturing sandwich composite webs from two adhesion-promoter-coated metal strips and an intermediate plastic web, emphasizing continuous processing and the separation of coating and laminating operations.
counterfactuals.output:
### Technical Invention Summary

The invention concerns a continuous method and production system for manufacturing sandwich composite webs comprising two metal cover strips and an intermediate plastic web. Each metal strip is provided, on the surface facing the plastic core, with an adhesion-promoter coating.

A principal feature is the physical and temporal separation of the coating operation from the laminating operation. In a first continuous processing stage, the metal strips are unwound, cleaned or pretreated as required, coated with an adhesion promoter, and dried, cured, or otherwise conditioned. The coated strips may then be rewound, buffered, stored, or transferred to a separate production line.

In a subsequent continuous laminating stage, the two pre-coated metal strips are unwound independently and conveyed toward a laminating zone. A continuously supplied or extruded plastic web is introduced between the mutually facing adhesion-promoter-coated surfaces. The three layers are brought together under controlled temperature and pressure, for example by heated rollers, a double-belt press, or a calendering unit, to activate the adhesion promoter and form a bonded sandwich composite web. The resulting laminate can be cooled, edge-trimmed, inspected, and wound or cut to length.

Separating coating from lamination allows each operation to be performed under independently optimized speed, temperature, atmosphere, and curing conditions. It also avoids exposing the plastic web to coating solvents or coating-line conditions, reduces interruptions of the laminating line, and permits quality control and inventory management of the pre-coated metal strips before assembly. Continuous web handling throughout both stages provides high throughput, uniform bond quality, and scalable manufacture of metal–plastic–metal composite webs.
